voices.2: Kokoro am_michael, base speed 0.85, directed per passage (render_kokoro.py)

tracks.title: An orangery for a garden
tracks.where: Outside the museum, at its west end, the Concorde end of the Tuileries terrace, near the entrance.
tracks.what: The Orangerie of the Tuileries, built in 1852 on the orders of Napoleon III as a winter shelter for the garden's citrus trees, home to Monet's Water Lilies since 1927.
tracks.listen: Why a building made for orange trees was the right home for Monet, and how the visit unfolds.

tracks.title: A gift for the Armistice
tracks.where: In the entrance hall, just before you step into the first oval room of the Water Lilies.
tracks.what: The story of Monet's gift of the Water Lilies (Les Nymphéas) to the French State: offered in 1918, deed signed in 1922, rooms opened in 1927.
tracks.listen: How a two-painting gift, offered the day after the Armistice, grew into a building, and why Monet never saw it finished.

tracks.title: Inside the infinity
tracks.where: In the first oval room of the Water Lilies, standing near the middle, where you can turn and see all four compositions.
tracks.what: Claude Monet, Les Nymphéas (The Water Lilies), painted between 1914 and 1926: eight compositions on twenty-two panels, all two metres high and about ninety-one metres long in total, in two oval rooms. Four of them hang here.
tracks.listen: How the light, the shape of the rooms and the path of the sun were all part of Monet's plan.

tracks.title: Monet — Le Soleil couchant (Setting Sun)
tracks.where: In the first oval room, in front of the shortest of its four compositions, a single panel six metres wide.
tracks.what: Claude Monet, Le Soleil couchant (Setting Sun), from Les Nymphéas, 1914–1926, oil on one canvas panel, 200 × 600 cm.
tracks.listen: Why the smallest of the eight compositions is the only one on a single panel, and how the whole cycle follows the sun.

tracks.title: Monet — Les Nuages (Clouds)
tracks.where: In the first oval room, in front of one of its two longest compositions. Morning is the other, on the Seine side; Clouds is the long one that is not on the Seine side.
tracks.what: Claude Monet, Les Nuages (Clouds), from Les Nymphéas, 1914–1926, oil on canvas, 200 × 1275 cm.
tracks.listen: Clouds you can only see by looking down, and what was new about this cycle compared with the water lilies Monet had already shown.

tracks.title: Monet — Reflets verts (Green Reflections)
tracks.where: In the first oval room, in front of the composition of middle length, eight and a half metres wide; it is neither the single short panel nor one of the two longest.
tracks.what: Claude Monet, Reflets verts (Green Reflections), from Les Nymphéas, 1914–1926, oil on canvas, 200 × 850 cm.
tracks.listen: What these paintings have lived through since 1927, and where the water lilies come up out of the reflections.

tracks.title: Monet — Matin (Morning)
tracks.where: In the first oval room, in front of the long composition on the south wall, the Seine side of the room.
tracks.what: Claude Monet, Matin (Morning), from Les Nymphéas, 1914–1926, oil on canvas, 200 × 1275 cm.
tracks.listen: Why a room that runs from morning to evening ends with Morning, and what is waiting through the passage.

tracks.title: The willow room
tracks.where: Just inside the second oval room, having come through the passage from Room 1. Stand near the middle, where you can see all four compositions.
tracks.what: Room 2 of the Water Lilies: four compositions by Claude Monet, twelve panels, painted between 1914 and 1926, built on the contrast of weeping-willow branches against the water.
tracks.listen: What this second room is about, and the years of loss and war in which Monet painted it.

tracks.title: Monet — Reflets d'arbres (Reflections of Trees)
tracks.where: Room 2, on the end wall around the passage from Room 1. It's the shorter of the two end compositions; the much longer one faces it at the far end.
tracks.what: Claude Monet, Reflets d'arbres (Reflections of Trees), from the Water Lilies cycle, 1914–1926, oil on canvas, two panels, 200 × 850 cm.
tracks.listen: Why these paintings are part of the building itself, how this one was put together, and where the trees in the title really are.

tracks.room: Room 2 · north wall · Water Lilies · Ground floor
tracks.title: Monet — Le Matin aux saules (Morning with Willows)
tracks.where: Room 2, the north long wall: on your left as you face the far end of the room. One of the two long compositions that face each other across the room.
tracks.what: Claude Monet, Le Matin aux saules (Morning with Willows), from the Water Lilies cycle, 1914–1926, oil on canvas, three panels, 200 × 1275 cm.
tracks.listen: The real trees just beyond this wall, the studio where Monet painted it, and a new way to look at a painting too long to see from one spot.

tracks.room: Room 2 · south wall · Water Lilies · Ground floor
tracks.title: Monet — Le Matin clair aux saules (Clear Morning with Willows)
tracks.where: Room 2, the south long wall: on your right as you face the far end of the room, directly opposite Morning with Willows.
tracks.what: Claude Monet, Le Matin clair aux saules (Clear Morning with Willows), from the Water Lilies cycle, 1914–1926, oil on canvas, three panels of 200 × 425 cm, 200 × 1275 cm in all.
tracks.listen: Two mornings face to face, a looking game for one or two people, and the single word that separates them.

tracks.room: Room 2 · far end · Water Lilies · Ground floor
tracks.title: Monet — Les Deux Saules (The Two Willows)
tracks.where: Room 2, the end wall at the back of the room, facing you as you come in from Room 1. It's the longest composition in the museum.
tracks.what: Claude Monet, Les Deux Saules (The Two Willows), from the Water Lilies cycle, 1914–1926, oil on canvas, four panels, 200 × 1700 cm.
tracks.listen: Why the longest painting in the museum sits at the far end of the walk, which way it faces, and how to find the two trees of the title.

tracks.room: Room 2 · bench · Water Lilies · Ground floor
tracks.title: The last years
tracks.where: Sitting on a bench in the middle of Room 2, if one is free. Otherwise stand anywhere you can see the whole room.
tracks.what: Claude Monet's last years at Giverny: the cataract operation of 1923, the long struggle with his sight, and the panels he kept until his death in 1926.
tracks.listen: What Monet's eyes could still see when he finished these paintings, and how close he came to seeing them here.

tracks.room: Room 1 · on the way to the lower level · Ground floor
tracks.title: Hidden and found again
tracks.where: Back in Room 1 on your way out of the Water Lilies, anywhere you can look up at the pale ceiling, before you take the stairs or lift to the lower level.
tracks.what: The later history of the Water Lilies rooms: the upper floor built over them in the 1960s, and the 2000–2006 renovation that gave them back their daylight and moved the Walter-Guillaume collection below ground.
tracks.listen: How the Water Lilies lost their daylight for about forty years, how they got it back, and what the builders found underground.

tracks.room: Lower level · first hall of the collection
tracks.title: Paul Guillaume, the dealer
tracks.where: On the lower level, in the first hall of the Walter-Guillaume collection, among the large paintings that open the collection. Any spot with room to stand will do.
tracks.what: An introduction to Paul Guillaume, 1891–1934, the Paris dealer whose collection, completed by his widow Domenica, fills the lower level.
tracks.listen: How a young man with African sculptures in a garage window became the dealer of the Paris avant-garde, and the museum he dreamed of.

tracks.room: Lower level · first hall of the collection
tracks.title: Domenica and the State
tracks.where: Stay in the first hall of the Walter-Guillaume collection. Nothing in particular to face: this is the story of how the collection came to the nation.
tracks.what: Domenica Walter, born Juliette Lacaze, 1898–1977, widow of Paul Guillaume and later of the architect Jean Walter, and the state purchases that brought 146 paintings to the Orangerie.
tracks.listen: How a widow reshaped her husband's collection, sold it to France on her own terms, and gave it two men's names.

tracks.title: Modigliani — Paul Guillaume, Novo Pilota
tracks.where: On the lower level, in front of Modigliani's portrait of a young man in a dark suit and hat against a red background, with the words Novo Pilota at the lower left. Its room in the current hang is not confirmed; look among the large works at the start of the collection or with the other Modiglianis.
tracks.what: Amedeo Modigliani, Paul Guillaume, Novo Pilota, 1915, oil on cardboard mounted on plywood, 105 × 75 cm.
tracks.listen: What the painter wrote on his young dealer's portrait, and why.

tracks.title: Faces of a dealer — Derain and Van Dongen
tracks.where: On the lower level, wherever you find the portraits of Paul Guillaume and his wife: Derain's Guillaume in blue with a cigarette, Van Dongen's Guillaume in grey and blue, and Derain's Domenica in a large hat against a red curtain. They may hang apart, and the Van Dongen may not be on view.
tracks.what: André Derain, Portrait de Paul Guillaume, 1919, oil on canvas · Kees van Dongen, Portrait de Paul Guillaume, around 1930, oil on canvas, 100 × 74 cm · André Derain, Portrait de Madame Paul Guillaume au grand chapeau, 1928–29, oil on canvas, 92 × 73 cm.
tracks.listen: A dealer in blue with a dying cigarette, a dealer in grey with a new honour, and his wife in a great hat with a ghost behind her.

tracks.title: Renoir — Jeunes filles au piano (Young Girls at the Piano)
tracks.where: In the room of Renoir's paintings, in front of the upright canvas of two young girls at a piano, about 116 by 81 centimetres. Renoir's works toured abroad until early 2026 and the current hang is unconfirmed, so a work may be missing.
tracks.what: Pierre-Auguste Renoir, Jeunes filles au piano (Young Girls at the Piano), around 1892, oil on canvas, 116 × 81 cm.
tracks.listen: How Renoir's friends finally got the French state to buy him, and why this is the version he kept for himself.

tracks.title: Renoir — Yvonne et Christine Lerolle au piano
tracks.where: In the room of Renoir's paintings, in front of the horizontal canvas of two young women at a piano, one playing, one turning the pages, with two pictures hanging on the wall behind them. The current hang is unconfirmed, so it may be missing.
tracks.what: Pierre-Auguste Renoir, Yvonne et Christine Lerolle au piano (Yvonne and Christine Lerolle at the Piano), around 1897, oil on canvas, 73 × 92 cm.
tracks.listen: A musical household, two Degas paintings tucked into a Renoir, and why the family never owned their own portrait.

tracks.title: Renoir — Claude Renoir en clown (Claude Renoir as a Clown)
tracks.where: In the room of Renoir's paintings, in front of the portrait of a small boy in a red clown costume. The current hang is unconfirmed, so it may be missing.
tracks.what: Pierre-Auguste Renoir, Claude Renoir en clown (Claude Renoir as a Clown), 1909, oil on canvas.
tracks.listen: A boy who hated his costume, the bargain that got the portrait finished, and the old master Renoir was trying to match.

tracks.title: Renoir — Gabrielle et Jean (Gabrielle and Jean)
tracks.where: In the room of Renoir's paintings, in front of the small canvas of a young woman holding a little boy on her knee as he plays with toy animals on a table. The current hang is unconfirmed, so it may be missing.
tracks.what: Pierre-Auguste Renoir, Gabrielle et Jean (Gabrielle and Jean), 1895–1896, oil on canvas, 65 × 54 cm.
tracks.listen: The young woman who kept Renoir's baby son still long enough to be painted, and the cow you can barely recognise.

tracks.title: Renoir — Bathers and Gabrielle reclining
tracks.where: In the room of Renoir's paintings, in front of his nudes: a seated bather drying her leg on a white cloth by the water, a golden-haired bather drawing a white drape across her chest, and a long horizontal reclining nude. The current hang is unconfirmed, so one may be missing.
tracks.what: Pierre-Auguste Renoir, Femme nue dans un paysage (Nude in a Landscape), 1883, oil on canvas, 65 × 54 cm · Baigneuse aux cheveux longs (Bather with Long Hair), around 1895, oil on canvas, 82 × 65 cm · Femme nue couchée (Gabrielle) (Reclining Nude, Gabrielle), 1906, oil on canvas, 67 × 160 cm.
tracks.listen: How a trip to Italy sharpened Renoir's line, what the pearly period was, and how the family nanny became his Venus.

tracks.title: Renoir's quiet pictures
tracks.where: In the room of Renoir's paintings, among the smaller works: a little still life of apples and pears, a vase of tulips in reds, greens and yellows, and a snowy landscape. The current hang is unconfirmed, so one may be missing.
tracks.what: Pierre-Auguste Renoir, Pommes et poires (Apples and Pears), around 1895, 32 × 41 cm · Bouquet de tulipes (Bouquet of Tulips), around 1905, 44 × 37 cm · Paysage de neige (Snowy Landscape), around 1875, 51 × 66 cm; all oil on canvas.
tracks.listen: Three small pictures that show another Renoir: one learning from Cézanne, one in the southern light, and one working out the colour of snow.

tracks.title: Cézanne — Pommes et biscuits (Apples and Biscuits)
tracks.where: In the room of Cézanne's paintings, find a small still life of a plate and a few apples set on a chest. Cézannes from this collection are often lent out, and some may be away until early 2027.
tracks.what: Paul Cézanne, Pommes et biscuits (Apples and Biscuits), around 1880, oil on canvas. Bought by Domenica Walter at auction in Paris in 1952.
tracks.listen: The auction that made a widow's collection famous, the painting she and her husband bought in halves, and how Cézanne builds an apple out of colour.

tracks.title: Cézanne — Hortense: two portraits of Madame Cézanne
tracks.where: In the room of Cézanne's paintings, find the full-length woman in a garden, then the seated woman in a black dress against a blue-green ground. Either may be away on loan until early 2027.
tracks.what: Paul Cézanne, Madame Cézanne au jardin (Madame Cézanne in the Garden), around 1880, oil on canvas, 80 × 63 cm, and Portrait de Madame Cézanne (Portrait of Madame Cézanne), around 1885–1895, oil on canvas. Both bought by Paul Guillaume in the 1920s.
tracks.listen: Who Hortense Fiquet was, why her face gives nothing away, and what Cézanne was really after when he painted her.

tracks.title: Cézanne — Portrait du fils de l'artiste (Portrait of the Artist's Son)
tracks.where: In the room of Cézanne's paintings, find the small, close-cropped portrait of a boy, with just the back of an armchair at the right against a blue-green ground. Cézannes from this collection are often lent out; it may be away until early 2027.
tracks.what: Paul Cézanne, Portrait du fils de l'artiste (Portrait of the Artist's Son), around 1880, oil on canvas. Bought by Paul Guillaume in the 1920s.
tracks.listen: Three Pauls, one canvas, and how Cézanne builds a child's portrait out of rhyming curves.

tracks.title: Cézanne — Le Rocher rouge (The Red Rock)
tracks.where: In the room of Cézanne's paintings, find the upright landscape with an orange rock behind a patch of trees, topped by blue sky. It may be away on loan until early 2027.
tracks.what: Paul Cézanne, Le Rocher rouge (The Red Rock), around 1895, oil on canvas, 91 × 66 cm. Bought by Domenica Walter after Paul Guillaume's death.
tracks.listen: The deserted quarry Cézanne kept returning to, and the poet who saw young painters lining up behind him.

tracks.title: Cézanne — Trees and houses: three landscapes
tracks.where: In the room of Cézanne's paintings, find three landscapes: an upright view with a leaning tree trunk and a low wall, a hamlet among bare trees with pale houses, and the trees of the park at Château Noir. Any of them may be away on loan until early 2027.
tracks.what: Paul Cézanne, Paysage au toit rouge ou Le Pin à l'Estaque (Landscape with Red Roof, or The Pine at L'Estaque), 1875–76, oil on canvas, 73 × 60 cm · Arbres et maisons (Trees and Houses), around 1885, oil on canvas, 54 × 73 cm · Dans le parc de Château Noir (In the Park of Château Noir), 1898–1900, oil on canvas.
tracks.listen: Three landscapes, about twenty-five years apart, and how Cézanne learned from Pissarro and then let perspective dissolve.

tracks.title: Cézanne — Bathers and tables
tracks.where: In the room of Cézanne's paintings, find the long, narrow frieze of bathers around a boat, the tiny picnic scene with a church spire, and two still lifes: a straw-covered vase with a sugar bowl, and fruit with a napkin and a milk can. Any may be away on loan until early 2027.
tracks.what: Paul Cézanne, La Barque et les baigneurs (The Boat and the Bathers), around 1890, oil on canvas, 30 × 125 cm · Le Déjeuner sur l'herbe (Luncheon on the Grass), 1876–77, oil on canvas, 21 × 27 cm · Vase paillé, sucrier et pommes (Straw-covered Vase, Sugar Bowl and Apples), 1890–94, 36 × 46 cm · Fruits, serviette et boîte à lait (Fruit, Napkin and Milk Can), around 1880, 60 × 73 cm.
tracks.listen: A frieze cut into three and put back together, a picnic that may be a private joke, and two tables seen from impossible angles.

tracks.title: Rousseau — La Noce (The Wedding Party)
tracks.where: Among Henri Rousseau's paintings on the lower level; it may instead hang in the large first hall of the collection, with the big formats. Look for a tall group portrait of a wedding party in front of trees, with a dog in the foreground.
tracks.what: Henri Rousseau, La Noce (The Wedding Party), around 1905, oil on canvas. From Paul Guillaume's collection, acquired by the state from Domenica Walter in 1959.
tracks.listen: Who "the Douanier" really was, why there are no jungles here, and how a suburban wedding came to look like a sacred image.

tracks.title: Rousseau — La Carriole du père Junier (Old Junier's Cart)
tracks.where: Among Henri Rousseau's paintings on the lower level, find the wide picture of a family in a horse-drawn cart, pulled by a white mare, with three dogs.
tracks.what: Henri Rousseau, La Carriole du père Junier (Old Junier's Cart), 1908, oil on canvas, 97 × 129 cm.
tracks.listen: The neighbourhood grocer and his proud white mare, the painter on the front seat, and the dog that was too big on purpose.

tracks.title: Rousseau — L'Enfant à la poupée (Child with a Doll)
tracks.where: Among Henri Rousseau's paintings on the lower level, find the portrait of a child holding a doll.
tracks.what: Henri Rousseau, L'Enfant à la poupée (Child with a Doll), oil on canvas, Walter-Guillaume collection.
tracks.listen: Five francs in a junk shop, a banquet in Montmartre, and why this museum opens its collection with the modern "primitives".

tracks.title: Rousseau — Small worlds: anglers and a chair factory
tracks.where: Among Henri Rousseau's paintings on the lower level, find the anglers with an aeroplane in the sky and a factory chimney behind, and the chair factory, which the collection owns in two versions, one small.
tracks.what: Henri Rousseau, Les Pêcheurs à la ligne (The Anglers), 1908–09, oil on canvas · La Fabrique de chaises à Alfortville (The Chair Factory at Alfortville), 1897, oil on canvas · La Fabrique de chaises (The Chair Factory), a small version from around 1897, oil on canvas, 38 × 46 cm.
tracks.listen: An aeroplane over a quiet afternoon's fishing, and a factory that was painted precisely because nobody else would have.

tracks.title: Rousseau — Parks, cliffs and two new faces
tracks.where: Among Henri Rousseau's paintings on the lower level, look for a small park scene with walkers, a cliff, and possibly two small portraits on wood of a man and a woman, acquired in 2024. It is not confirmed which of these are on display.
tracks.what: Henri Rousseau, Promeneurs dans un parc (Walkers in a Park), between 1900 and 1910, oil on canvas, 46 × 55 cm · La Falaise (The Cliff), oil on canvas · Portrait d'homme and Portrait de femme (Portrait of a Man, Portrait of a Woman), 1887, small oils on wood, acquired in 2024.
tracks.listen: How nine Rousseaus became eleven, and an invitation to look without a guide's script.

tracks.title: Matisse — Les Trois Sœurs (The Three Sisters)
tracks.where: Among Matisse's paintings on the lower level. Look for a single upright canvas of three dark-haired young women seated close together against a plain brown background, two looking out, one reading.
tracks.what: Henri Matisse, Les Trois Sœurs (The Three Sisters), 1917, oil on canvas, 92 × 73 cm. One canvas, not a triptych: three other paintings of the same sisters are at the Barnes Foundation, Philadelphia.
tracks.listen: Why a dealer who sold the other three sisters to America bought this one at auction for himself.

tracks.title: Matisse — Rooms in Nice: Femmes au canapé and Le Boudoir
tracks.where: Among Matisse's paintings on the lower level. Look for a hotel interior with a large red curtain on the right, a tiled floor, a window onto the sky, and two lightly sketched women by a divan. Le Boudoir, a smaller interior, may hang nearby.
tracks.what: Henri Matisse, Femmes au canapé ou Le Divan (Women on a Sofa, or The Divan), 1921, oil on canvas. Also Le Boudoir (The Boudoir), oil on canvas.
tracks.listen: How Matisse turned an ordinary hotel room in Nice into a picture about being shut in and looking out.

tracks.title: Matisse — Femme au violon and Femme à la mandoline
tracks.where: Among Matisse's paintings on the lower level. Look for a small canvas of a seated young woman with a violin on her knees, against a screen patterned with blue circles; the Woman with a Mandolin may hang near it.
tracks.what: Henri Matisse, Femme au violon (Woman with a Violin), 1921–1922, oil on canvas, 55 × 46 cm. Also Femme à la mandoline (Woman with a Mandolin), oil on canvas, early 1920s.
tracks.listen: A painting with a twin in Baltimore, and what music meant in Matisse's Nice.

tracks.title: Matisse — The Odalisques
tracks.where: Among Matisse's paintings on the lower level. Look for the reclining and seated women among screens, curtains and patterned fabric: a nude in blue tones before a Moorish screen, a nude on a white sheet before a red curtain, and the odalisques in red and in grey trousers.
tracks.what: Henri Matisse, Odalisque bleue ou L'Esclave blanche (Blue Odalisque, or The White Slave) · Nu drapé étendu (Reclining Draped Nude), 1923–1924 · Odalisque à la culotte rouge (Odalisque with Red Trousers) · Odalisque à la culotte grise (Odalisque with Grey Trousers), 1926–1927. All oil on canvas, all from Paul Guillaume's collection.
tracks.listen: Why the critics sneered at Matisse's odalisques, and what he was really painting.

tracks.title: Picasso — L'Étreinte (The Embrace)
tracks.where: Among Picasso's works on the lower level. Look for a tall pastel of a nude man and woman embracing in a bedroom, in blues and pinks. It is a light-sensitive work lent by the Louvre and may not be on the wall.
tracks.what: Pablo Picasso, L'Étreinte (The Embrace), 1903, pastel, 98 × 57 cm. Musée du Louvre, Department of Prints and Drawings, on long-term loan to the Orangerie (first inventoried RF 1960-34).
tracks.listen: A Blue Period embrace made in Barcelona, in a studio full of grief, and the larger picture it led to.

tracks.title: Picasso — Les Adolescents and Nu sur fond rouge
tracks.where: Among Picasso's works on the lower level; large works may hang in the collection's opening hall. Look for a big canvas of two nude young figures on a pink-ochre ground, one with a pitcher on her head, and a smaller nude against a flat red background.
tracks.what: Pablo Picasso, Les Adolescents (The Adolescents), 1906, oil on canvas, 157 × 117 cm. Also Nu sur fond rouge (Nude against a Red Background), late 1906, oil on canvas, 81 × 54 cm.
tracks.listen: The ghost of an abandoned picture under two young nudes, and the red nude that points straight at Les Demoiselles d'Avignon.

tracks.title: Picasso — Femme au peigne, Composition : paysans, Femme au chapeau blanc
tracks.where: Among Picasso's works on the lower level. Look for a large gouache of a standing nude combing long black hair, a gouache of a father with his hand on his daughter's shoulder under a garland of flowers, and a seated woman in a white hat. Works on paper are rotated and may be resting.
tracks.what: Pablo Picasso, Femme au peigne (Woman with a Comb), 1906, gouache on paper · Composition : paysans (Composition: Peasants), 1906, gouache on paper, 70 × 50 cm · Femme au chapeau blanc (Woman in a White Hat), 1921, oil on canvas, 118 × 91 cm.
tracks.listen: The Picasso Domenica refused to sell, a tender study for a picture now in Philadelphia, and a quiet woman who may be his first wife.

tracks.title: Picasso — Grande baigneuse (Large Bather)
tracks.where: Among Picasso's works on the lower level; as a very large canvas it may hang in the collection's opening hall. Look for a monumental seated nude with massive, statue-like limbs; nearby, a seated nude holding a drape, and two small studies of women at a fountain.
tracks.what: Pablo Picasso, Grande baigneuse (Large Bather), 1921–22, oil on canvas, 182 × 101.5 cm. Also Grand nu à la draperie (Large Nude with Drapery), 1921–1923, 160 × 95 cm, and two studies for Femmes à la fontaine (Women at the Fountain), 1921, oil on canvas.
tracks.listen: Why Picasso turned from Cubism to giant classical women, and the small change of pose you can catch him deciding.

tracks.title: Picasso — Femme au tambourin (Woman with a Tambourine)
tracks.where: Among Picasso's works on the lower level. Look for a wide canvas of a woman reclining on cushions, propped on one elbow and holding a tambourine, in mauve, yellow, garnet red and turquoise; nearby, a Cubist still life of a compote dish, bottle and glass on a tilted beige tabletop.
tracks.what: Pablo Picasso, Femme au tambourin (Woman with a Tambourine), 1925, oil on canvas, 97 × 130 cm. Also Grande nature morte (Large Still Life), 1917, oil on canvas, 87 × 116 cm.
tracks.listen: How Paul Guillaume set Picasso against Matisse, and how this reclining woman answers Matisse's odalisques.

tracks.title: Modigliani — Le Jeune Apprenti (The Young Apprentice)
tracks.where: Among Modigliani's portraits on the lower level. Look for a tall canvas of a seated young man in greys and browns, his head resting on one hand, a white collar and intensely blue eyes.
tracks.what: Amedeo Modigliani, Le Jeune Apprenti (The Young Apprentice), 1917–1919 (museum page; also given as 1918–19), oil on canvas, 100 × 65 cm, RF 1963-71.
tracks.listen: A nameless young man from the south, painted near the end of Modigliani's short life, and the two blue notes that hold the whole picture.

tracks.title: Soutine — Le Petit Pâtissier (The Little Pastry Cook)
tracks.where: In the room of Soutine's paintings, in front of a small portrait of a thin young cook in a white pastry cook's hat and jacket, holding a flat, bright red cloth.
tracks.what: Chaïm Soutine, Le Petit Pâtissier, The Little Pastry Cook, around 1922–23, oil on canvas, 73 × 54 cm. Jean Walter and Paul Guillaume collection.
tracks.listen: How a painting of a pastry cook made Soutine's name in America, and why Paul Guillaume bought this one years later.

tracks.title: Soutine — Le Garçon d'étage and La Fiancée
tracks.where: In the room of Soutine's paintings. Look for a hotel waiter in a red waistcoat, standing with his hands on his hips, then a tall, narrow portrait of a thin young woman in a white dress.
tracks.what: Chaïm Soutine, Le Garçon d'étage, The Room-Service Waiter, around 1927, oil on canvas, 87 × 66 cm; La Fiancée, The Bride, around 1923, oil on canvas; La Jeune Anglaise, The Young Englishwoman, 1934, oil on canvas.
tracks.listen: The hotel staff nobody looked at, the year Soutine's red took over, and a bride squeezed into her frame.

tracks.title: Soutine — Bœuf et tête de veau and Le Lapin
tracks.where: In the room of Soutine's paintings, in front of the still lifes of meat: a side of beef beside a calf's head against a dark ground, and a tall, narrow picture of a rabbit hanging by one leg beside a red jug.
tracks.what: Chaïm Soutine, Bœuf et tête de veau, Side of Beef and Calf's Head, oil on canvas; Le Lapin, The Rabbit, 1923–24, oil on canvas, 73 × 36 cm; and Dindon et tomates, Turkey and Tomatoes, oil on canvas.
tracks.listen: Why the most violent painter in the building had such old-fashioned heroes, Rembrandt and Chardin.

tracks.title: Soutine — Houses that move: Le Village and the landscapes
tracks.where: In the room of Soutine's paintings, in front of the landscapes: villages and roads whose houses lean and twist. Le Village is the most tangled of them.
tracks.what: Chaïm Soutine, Le Village, The Village, 1923, oil on canvas; with Les Maisons, The Houses, and Paysage avec personnage, Landscape with Figure, both oil on canvas.
tracks.listen: Soutine's years in Céret and Cagnes, the landscape the museum calls his most radical, and the end of his story.

tracks.title: Derain — Arlequin et Pierrot (Harlequin and Pierrot)
tracks.where: In the room of André Derain's paintings, in front of the large picture of two costumed musicians with guitars: Harlequin in a chequered suit and two-cornered hat, Pierrot all in white with a ruff and a black skullcap.
tracks.what: André Derain, Arlequin et Pierrot, Harlequin and Pierrot, around 1924, oil on canvas, commissioned by Paul Guillaume. Jean Walter and Paul Guillaume collection.
tracks.listen: The dealer who commissioned a painting and ended up inside it, and the hired model who complicates the story.

tracks.title: Derain — The painter's niece, and a Harlequin alone
tracks.where: In the room of André Derain's paintings. Look for the life-size portrait of a girl in a white dress against browns and yellows, and the tall, life-size Harlequin playing a guitar.
tracks.what: André Derain, La Nièce du peintre, The Painter's Niece, and La Nièce du peintre assise, The Painter's Niece, Seated, both oil on canvas; Arlequin à la guitare, Harlequin with a Guitar, 1924, oil on canvas, 190 × 97 cm.
tracks.listen: The baby who moved into Derain's house and sat for him more than a hundred times, and the hired model in Harlequin's costume.

tracks.title: Derain — La Table de cuisine (The Kitchen Table) and the still lifes
tracks.where: In the room of André Derain's paintings, in front of the large, dark still life of kitchen utensils on a table, painted mostly in browns. His smaller still lifes of fruit, bread, jugs and baskets hang nearby.
tracks.what: André Derain, La Table de cuisine, The Kitchen Table, around 1922–25, oil on canvas; with Nature morte champêtre, Rustic Still Life, Nature morte au panier, Still Life with Basket, Nature morte au verre de vin, Still Life with a Glass of Wine, and Poires et cruche, Pears and Jug.
tracks.listen: Why critics thought of Caravaggio in front of a kitchen table, and the difference between a finished picture and a sketch.

tracks.title: Derain — Nudes and the light of Provence
tracks.where: In the room of André Derain's paintings, among his nudes and his landscapes of Provence: hill villages, a road under a deep blue sky, plane trees under a stormy one.
tracks.what: André Derain, nudes including Le Beau Modèle, The Beautiful Model, 1923, Le Modèle blond, The Blond Model, Grand nu couché, Large Reclining Nude, and Nu au canapé, Nude on a Sofa; landscapes including La Route, The Road, and Arbres et village, Trees and Village, both 1932, and two Paysages de Provence. All oil on canvas.
tracks.listen: Derain talking back to the old masters in his nudes, and one Provençal village seen in two weathers.

tracks.room: Room 1 or 2 · Water Lilies · Ground floor
tracks.title: A second look at the Water Lilies
tracks.where: Back on the ground floor, in either of the two oval Water Lilies rooms. Find a bench or a quiet spot facing whichever composition you like best.
tracks.what: Claude Monet, Les Nymphéas, The Water Lilies: eight compositions on twenty-two panels, painted between 1914 and 1926, oil on canvas, two metres high.
tracks.listen: Why the same paintings look different now, and how the collection downstairs once hung over Monet's head.

tracks.title: Into the Tuileries
tracks.where: Outside, on or just beyond the footbridge from the museum's garden-side exit, with the Tuileries garden in front of you and the building behind.
tracks.what: The Musée de l'Orangerie, built in 1852 as a winter shelter for the Tuileries orange trees; its garden-side exit, opened during the 2025 works; and Monet's gift of the Water Lilies.
tracks.listen: Why this side of the building was almost blind for so long, how a two-painting gift became a whole museum, and a goodbye.
